messages.author: LSE Group
messages.content: Hello everyone, We’re pleased to share a special announcement for all teams working with GitLab in hosted or corporate environments. Mnemosyne is our new product, built to meet the need for a central, team-wide AI documentation system. Instead of keeping development notes locally, Mnemosyne stores them on a server, organized per project and shared across every AI model your team uses. Teams can work on projects faster, and every model has access to the same central notes through SSO authentication and MCP access via Streamable HTTPS. Our development team is spread across a dozen time zones, so we know the challenges of distributed work firsthand. Mnemosyne also addresses a growing concern for management: staying compliant without extra effort, and keeping disaster recovery and project documentation current at the push of a button, powered by AI. Mnemosyne began as a standalone MCP project. During this Hackathon Challenge, we are extending it with a full web interface and SSO system. Together with MUSE AI and other AI interfaces, teams can create workflows, build Wikipedia-style documentation, and generate complete disaster recovery PDF documents at the click of a button. Pending the executive decision at the end of November, the project will remain open source, so anyone who wants their own copy can fork it. We wish all participants the best of luck. https://github.com/lsegroup/mnemosyne

messages.author: WAYNE LEVI
messages.content: Update on Vee Vee — she's still free and live, and now her homework is public. Her instruction core just passed an 89-question exam at 89/89 on Muse Wonder — then the identical, unchanged instructions passed 89/89 again on a second brain, Muse Spark 1.3. Same sheet, two brains, full marks both times. The full record is in the repo as PROOF.md — including the failed first run, what she got wrong, and the exact fixes that earned the pass. I didn't hide the miss. She also got a design map (ARCHITECTURE.md) and a first screen that shows her systems with buttons to test them yourself. Live: https://wayneherrington.github.io/veevee/ Repo: https://github.com/wayneherrington/veevee Ask her something she can't know. She'll check — or she'll tell you she couldn't find it. That was the whole point of building her. — Wayne (solo builder, first build of my life)

messages.author: Tian
messages.content: Hi everyone! I’m Tian, a full-stack developer with 9+ years of experience shipping web apps and AI products (Next.js, TypeScript, Python, PostgreSQL, LLM APIs, plus agent tooling like Hermes and OpenClaw). I’m building an AI grading assistant for handwritten exams for the “Build for Your World” theme: snap a photo of an answer sheet, split it into answer areas, grade each against a rubric, and return per-student scores with feedback, with the teacher always having the final say. It’s a problem I know firsthand, and I’ll share a working demo here as soon as it’s live: [link GitHub/demo]. I’m looking for 1–2 teammates, ideally someone strong in vision/handwriting recognition, or someone who can help with design and the demo video. DM me if that’s you!

messages.author: John
messages.content: Hi all 👋 I'm Raj, founder of Lexcore Enterprises (India). We build and ship Android AI apps — a few are live on Google Play (Naira AI, Thali Calorie, Clay Music). For this hackathon (Startup track, Build for Your World) I'm building SayLedger by Cortina: a voice + vision ledger agent for small shops. Speak an entry, snap an old handwritten ledger page, ask "how much credit is outstanding?" — Muse Voice Transcribe + Muse Spark + SAM 3.1, with all the maths done in code, never by the model. Happy to swap feedback with other builders working on small-business or voice tools!
